quest.title: Where the Moon Rises
quest.description: Moonlight paves your way, guiding you to Nod-Krai, an "elysium" for adventurers and wanderers alike...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act I
chapter.title: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Eh? Well, well, if it isn't the ineffable Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hello there, Demyan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know each other?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Of course! Ineffa's a regular here at The Flagship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So robots are into booze too?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Not at all. The energy conversion efficiency of alcoholic drinks is very low, and most of them are full of impurities. Still, I can affirm that your Berries and Fried Meat deserve a solid 9.12/10. It has Aino's approval, too.

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Funny that you should mention that — while you were away in Natlan, Varka would come in here every day to pick up a serving of Berries and Fried Meat for Aino.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, he must have been worried sick that she wasn't eating properly on account of being so hung up about Ineffa being gone...

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Uh... Actually, it's 'cause Varka found out that Aino went wild after Ineffa left, gorging herself on snacks she normally couldn't get her hands on. So it was more... worry that she wasn't getting a balanced diet.

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: #Ahaha... Think I might've just put my foot in it. Anyway, since you're back from Natlan, these two must be the ones Varka mentioned... {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that's us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, from the sounds of it, you must be a close friend of Varka's too?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Varka? Ha-ha, goes without saying! After all, he's the only one around here who's ever managed to stay standing after ten rounds of the Roulette Special!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe he's made such a name for himself, though guess it's hardly surprising how...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know where he is now?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: Right now... Hmm... Must be somewhere near Amsvartnir. That's... quite far from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where's that?

dialogues.speaker: Demyan
dialogues.text: It's a lake in the northern part of Nod-Krai. Word reached him of trouble brewing around those parts, so he took his knights to check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So we missed him?

choices.text: Typical Mondstadter, coming and going like the wind...

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: Haha... Varka knew you'd say that, so he specifically told me to make sure you stayed here and enjoyed yourselves. He sends his assurances that everything's under control.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if he's that confident, guess our only option is to accept. Anyway, it's not like there's any special cause for concern — he is the Grand Master, after all.

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: Exactly. Plus, not only has he booked you into our finest room, he's paid for it in advance too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's so generous of him! Hehe. We might not have met yet, but Paimon's got a feeling that we'll get along with Varka like a house on fire...

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: Oh, and by the way, he also asked me to serve up a portion of Berries and Fried Meat for Ineffa. That was prepaid as well.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Demyan
response.text: No, thank you. I'm the one who should be grateful for your business.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, why don't you go ahead and drop off your luggage? I can use this time to go pick up some components that Aino asked me to bring back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! Besides, now that we've got ourselves a map, once we're done unpacking, we might as well go for a stroll ourselves! Why don't we meet up again later?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Oh, so you no longer require navigational assistance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No worries, we should be fine! We've got a rough idea of our way round town, so Paimon's reasonably confident we shouldn't get too lost...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Thank you. This translates into an approximate time saving of 30%, meaning I will be able to see Aino about 45 minutes earlier than previously projected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, you must miss her a lot too. In that case, we'd better get a move on!

choices.text: Do you think he needs our help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Ineffa! Sorry to keep you waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That is perfectly alright. My data indicates clear skies in the coming days. Current conditions for maritime travel: optimal. I will be ready whenever you are.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's get this show on the whale-road.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... are we really gonna set off without telling anyone again?

choices.text: Isn't that just how we roll?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, funny you mention it, you'll never guess who Paimon saw on the way o—

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hey! You didn't seriously think we'd let you leave without a farewell party, did you? ... No chance!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #Yeah, c'mon, {NICKNAME}! We've already made all the preparations.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: And most importantly... How dare you try and slip away without first paying your respects to the Almighty Dragonlord!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Caught red-handed, again...

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: A little bird told us you'd soon be leaving for Nod-Krai, so we asked Paimon to give us a heads-up before the date of your departure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...So it was you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you sure it's not time to think about changing that little habit of ours?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Don't worry, we won't keep you long. Besides, everyone's there already! Chasca, Iansan, Ororon... even the Pyro Archon herself!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: You're invited too, Ineffa! Xilonen has a special gift for you, hehe.

choices.text: Can't refuse an invitation like that...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Accompaniment request accepted. Xilonen demonstrates excellent massage technique. My impression of her is exceedingly positive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... so robots like massages too? Or is it just that Xilonen really knows how you're wired...?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Alright, enough with the chit-chat. Let's head to the venue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woohoo, party time!

choices.text: How about you, Ineffa?
When we're not being tailed by star Fontainian reporters, that is...

dialogues.text: Mm? Spit it out, then.
...They've set off.
Heh... Just as my calculations projected.
About time I met this "variable" in person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...You know, every time we head to a new nation, there's always a point where it suddenly dawns on Paimon: "This is it — the next chapter of our adventure has begun."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This time, it was the moment she realized she'd just polished off the very last of her Saurus Crackers. Should've stocked up better at the farewell party...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: In other words, Paimon has marked the geographic coordinates from two minutes and forty seconds ago as the boundary between Natlan and Nod-Krai. This deviates somewhat from the official coordinates stored in my database.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uhh, Paimon meant more in terms of how it felt on a psychological level... Anyway, what about you, {NICKNAME}? When did it really sink in for you?

choices.text: When I could no longer see qucusaurs soaring through the sky...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that actually kinda makes sense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you, Ineffa? Come to think of it, maybe we should be asking the other way round... So, when you came over to Natlan, what was the moment you felt like you'd left Nod-Krai?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Hmm. In that case, probably when my sensors could no longer detect the moon's power.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The moon? You mean... that one we can all see in the sky...?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #Negative, I was referring to... Ah, here we are. Paimon, {NICKNAME}, we have arrived in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh wow!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}, welcome to Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That must be Nasha Town up ahead! That's the place you were telling us about on the way over, right?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: That is correct, Paimon. It is also the most bustling commercial hub in all of Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...! Could this really be...?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh! Hehe, sounds like the perfect place to start trying out all the local specialties...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh? Is something up, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #This is where our spaceship landed when {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} and I first arrived in Teyvat...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A—Are you sure? But... how come you've never mentioned that before? Seems pretty important to Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Well, because... those memories are really hazy. All I remember is {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} waking me up, and us leaving the ship...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But just now, setting foot on this land... I felt something... The kind of power I sensed in those moments...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Are you referring to kuuvahki?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kuuvah-what now!?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: The locals refer to it as "kuuvahki." It is a unique elemental force found only in Nod-Krai — or rather, a pure, primordial form of elemental energy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A bit like phlogiston?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: That is correct. Another similar concept I have found in my database is: "the Primordial Sea."

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Legend has it that long, long ago, the moon that shines in the sky above us once rose from the land of Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Modern geological surveys and meteorite studies conducted in the region have since supported this claim.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, when you mentioned being able to detect the moon's power earlier... You were referring to "kuuvahki"?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It certainly feels similar to phlogiston, yet also somehow... different. Maybe they both belong to the "Light Realm" that the Lord of the Night mentioned...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Still, this feeling... There's no doubt about it — it's the same power I felt the first time I set foot in Teyvat...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, {NICKNAME}! You're saying... we might actually find your spaceship here? Do you still remember where it landed?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think it was... near a beach?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Nod-Krai is surrounded by the ocean — in other words, it could have been anywhere along its coastline.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There was also... a mountain?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Mm... Negative. Description still lacks sufficient detail to pinpoint target location.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, it's okay if you can't remember everything right away. After all, it's been a really long time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's just do what we've always done... and keep searching as we explore! Besides, what have you got to fear with your sidekick Paimon still here?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I'd be more than happy to help you out as well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you both...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Our pleasure! Anyway, just knowing that your spaceship's here in Nod-Krai surely counts as a big step forward, huh?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Like we've crossed another "boundary"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon couldn't have put it better herself. You sure are a quick learner, Ineffa!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If we can find our spaceship, maybe the flight logs could tell us something...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (At last, a chance to get to the bottom of all this... The truth must be out there somewhere, buried in this land.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem! Well, as the best guide in the whole of Teyvat, Paimon hereby does solemnly declare:

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nod-Krai, here we come!

choices.text: When I could no longer sense the flow of phlogiston...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It just occurred to Paimon — if we were looking to put out a "Missing Spaceship" commission or to learn more about Nod-Krai, wouldn't it make sense to drop by the Adventurers' Guild?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The Guild is located in Nasha Town. Simply follow this road and you'll reach it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What in Teyvat is that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks kinda like a Seelie, floating around in the air like that...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That is a kuuhenki, a species unique to the land of Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A kuuhenki? Does she have something to do with the moon, too?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Indeed, it does. According to the Frostmoon Scions, the indigenous inhabitants of this land, the kuuhenki are said to be familiars of the Moon Goddess, leading those who walk in the moonlight's glow to things of great importance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Moon Goddess? Don't all people here worship the Tsaritsa...?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Although Nod-Krai lies on Snezhnaya's border regions, the people here have held their own unique beliefs since time immemorial. As I mentioned, everything in this land shares a deep connection with the moon in the sky above.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The beliefs of the Frostmoon Scions seem to date back to the civilization of the angels. According to the documents in my database, even the Seven Archons did not exist at that time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... So the origin of their beliefs goes back even further than the Archon War?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Correct. At some point, you may come across some statues of their goddess — the Frostmoon Scions carved these as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, looks like she's floating away!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I suggest you follow her. The probability of an ordinary person encountering a kuuhenki lies in the single digits. Many here consider them heralds of good fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Hey, look! Isn't that Lauma... the Moonchanter?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let me take a look at your wound... *sigh* You must be more careful. Doesn't matter how much of a rush you're in — your safety always comes first.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Oh? You're back too. How was your day?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You what...? Those two Fatui, the ones who were causing trouble in Nasha Town... You went to teach them a lesson? And your... you put that in their food?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...You naughty little thing! How could you do that?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They didn't notice? That's not the point... You mustn't do that again, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Next time, at the very least, bring a few of your friends along too. You'll be an easy target if it's just you on your own!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Lauma! Still remember us?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Oh, it's {NICKNAME} and Paimon, isn't it? Welcome to Hiisi Island!

choices.text: Sorry for just showing up like this, out of the blue.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Not at all. Those who come with kindness in their hearts are always welcome with the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Were you just talking to those animals...?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I was indeed. The Frostmoon Scions' bloodline is unique — for throughout our history, there have been many among us who could communicate with all living things.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Hmm...? What was that? Oh, is that so?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: She says she was trapped in a plant earlier, and that you were the ones who rescued her. She wants me to thank you on her behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it was nothing! Barely lifted a finger.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If you both are free, why don't you join us at the Frostmoon Enclave for dinner? Consider it a small token of thanks for your kindness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'd love to! And actually, we had something we wanted to ask you anyway.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This statue...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Oh? You're interested in the story of "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Kuutar?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Yes. Kuutar is our Moon Goddess — the Moon Maiden who guides us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But up close, this one somehow seems a bit different from the one in Nasha Town. It's like it's more...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...Natural?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Or like... more harmonized in its design?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Mm... That is because, ever since the Fatui arrived in Nod-Krai, they have been modifying and defacing our statues as they please.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: These statues were made by the Frostmoon Scions who settled here hundreds of years ago, crafted from the very finest Lunasoul Stone.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Not only is this stone exceedingly rare, but it also brims with kuuvahki. I suppose the latter must be what caught the Fatui's eye.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: For a time, we put up fierce resistance... but now, this is the only one left that still retains her original form.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard they even pulled some Ancient Moon's Remnants down from the sky!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: That's right. The two largest remnants landed in Nod-Krai — one here on Hiisi Island, and the other on Paha Isle.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The Fatui built their research facility on top of the remnant over on Paha Isle, but they've had their sights set on the one here too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! Oh, it's that little kuuhenki again!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Surely that can't be...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, we've been wondering what was up with it too! It just appeared out of some petals and hasn't stopped following us since.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: No, that is no ordinary kuuhenki. These we name "Luonnotar," beings born from the Moon Goddess's blessing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can you understand what it's saying? We honestly haven't got the slightest idea why it's been following us...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: ...I'm afraid not. I cannot fathom its thinking any better than you can.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Sometimes, a long time must elapse before the Moon Goddess's blessings turn into Luonnotar. Perhaps you two were simply there to witness that transformation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, maybe...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Legend has it that the Luonnotar bring good fortune. Given that it seems to have taken a liking to you both, why don't you let it come along with you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Hehe, then you can start by helping us find some more treasure chests along the way... Capiche?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Mmm... Twilight approaches.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If you would hear more of the moons' story, then let us make our way to the Frostmoon Enclave. Beneath the gentle moonlight, I shall share this tale in full.

choices.text: Hope we're not imposing on you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this... a travel guide? Huh, it actually led us to something useful.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Are there any particular points of interest?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It all looks pretty interesting to Paimon! If we have time, she'd love to see... pretty much everything...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Recalibrating route...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: If we keep following the current path, we will arrive at an area of scenic beauty. From there, we will be able to identify both the Adventurers' Guild and several must-visit specialty stores.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes... Why is Paimon suddenly getting the feeling that, if she doesn't step it up soon, Ineffa's gonna put her out of a job...

talks.objective: Familiarize yourself with Nasha Town with Ineffa as your guide

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Nasha Town actually looks pretty big from here! Feels a bit different than Paimon imagined, though...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Which aspects in particular deviated from your expectations?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Paimon keeps hearing people describe Nod-Krai as an "adventurers' paradise," so she kinda thought it'd be a bit more... picture-perfect, somehow?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: According to legend, there was indeed an era of peace in Nod-Krai's past — the age of the Fae.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Tales of those ancient heroes are still told today. One of the most well-known is that of the Lantern Fae.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This individual performed many good deeds for Nod-Krai. The present-day Lightkeepers' nightly lantern patrols are, in part, a tribute to their memory. But then, one day...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What happened...?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...There came a devastating Abyssal calamity that swept across Nod-Krai, and for a time, it was left desolate.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Heartbroken by what had become of the land they had so cherished, that Fae extinguished their light, just as the Abyss had extinguished all hope.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Nowadays, the "paradise" people speak of is more of an aspiration — or an irony, perhaps.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An irony...?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Today, no official authority governs Nod-Krai. In theory, at least, it is somewhere a person can do whatever they wish, and become whoever they want to be.

choices.text: So it's a lawless paradise.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: The Adventurers' Guild is just over there, in Nasha Town's central plaza, and The Flagship Tavern is over that way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what's that building over there? Y'know, the biggest, tallest one?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: That is Aino's "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Energy Cannon." It gets activated when the Wild Hunt threat level outside Nasha Town reaches a certain threshold.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But according to the scan I just ran, the Energy Cannon appears to be malfunctioning... likely due to a recent discharge.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Wild Hunt... Isn't that the Abyssal calamity you mentioned that's specific to Nod-Krai?

choices.text: Does it pose a great threat to the people living here?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: It is a phenomenon that has been occurring for several centuries now, yet the time and location of Wild Hunt attacks are seemingly random. At first, it was more of an old wives' tale that adults used to scare children.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: "If you don't start behaving, kid, some night, the Wild Hunt's gonna come for you. Listen... Do you hear that? That weeping in the fog... Those are the cries of a young woman being dragged away."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You're saying people actually hear things like that?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I have not witnessed enough Wild Hunt attacks to give a statistically sound answer.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But the oldest legends say that all people saw was the ghostly shadow of a woman in the mist. It wasn't until later that it became a full-blown calamity, Abyssal monsters and all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When you put it like that, Paimon's really gotta hand it to Aino... Not only did she repair you, but she's even built a giant cannon to keep the Wild Hunt at bay!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Absolutely. Aino is very impressive indeed.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Anyway, according to my schedule, it is time I took you over to The Flagship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, sure! After all, we shouldn't keep Varka waiting. Though... Paimon's not sure if he'll actually show up at the bar this early.

choices.text: Have faith in the people of Mondstadt, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh. You're right about that...

choices.text: As far as they're concerned, any o'clock is bar o'clock.
Does it happen often?
So it's a paradise of freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Here we are, The Flagship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Varka told us to meet him here in his letter, right? Let's see... Varka! Varka...!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...No matches identified.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so he isn't here after all? Guess we never did actually say we'd be arriving today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, why don't we go ask the owner? If what they say is true, Varka's drinking prowess must have left quite the impression...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, feels pretty nice having someone sort out our food and lodging for us, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But is this really The Flagship's best room? It's pretty big, make no mistake — but it looks a little... worn out, right? Though, to be perfectly honest, that feels right at home with everything else we've seen of Nasha Town...

choices.text: A town built among ruins...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean it's got something to do with Nod-Krai's history? That makes sense... but what exactly was this calamity?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we try the Berries and Fried Meat too? Paimon's getting hungrier and hungrier every time someone mentions it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, oooh! Sorry about that, Paimon wasn't watching where she was going!
Please, there's no need to apologize. If anything, I'm the one who should be sorry — clearly, I shouldn't have gotten lost in my thoughts in the middle of a hallway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a sec... Are you staying in the room next to ours?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, quite the perceptive one, I see. First things first, allow me to introduce myself: My name is Kyryll Chudomirovich Flins. But please, just call me Flins.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's... an impressively long name, for sure!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Oh, is that so? Names like mine ought to have been fairly common in Snezhnaya, at least in the past. Would I be correct, then, to assume that the two of you are travelers in this land?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yep, you sure would be! Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. We've been to a bunch of nations already, but we only just arrived in Nod-Krai today.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hello.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: What a rare honor it is to meet such worldly travelers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you here for travel too?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Ah, if only I had the time to spare. No, I'm just staying the night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? So you're here for business?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: That's certainly one way to put it. I'm a Ratnik of Nod-Krai, normally stationed near the burial grounds to the north. My sole cause for being here today was to repair this lantern of mine.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's something off about that lantern...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—Burial g—g—grounds?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Your surprise is entirely understandable. Most people cannot even begin to fathom the idea of a life surrounded by tombstones and decay.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But if you've heard of the calamitous abomination that is the Wild Hunt, you'll know that in their wake, they bring a host of souls tainted by Abyssal filth. That, then, is why we are stationed by the burial grounds — to hold the line where it is most vulnerable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhh, so it's all about fighting against the Abyss... Sounds like a tough job.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: I thank you for your concern. But in truth, I've long since grown used to it — in fact, I like to think it rather suits me. If anything, I'd say I prefer the peace and quiet of a graveyard to the hustle and bustle of urban life.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon sort of gets it now, but even so, she's still pretty sure she could never get used to living in a graveyard herself... For one thing, she'd be too scared to fall asleep at night!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hahaha... Oh, I assure you, there's no need to worry on that account. The kind of ghosts you find in cemeteries aren't too big on talking — but even when they do, they're usually far more discreet than the living.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, would you look at that? Who'd have thought we'd end up chatting this long. Must have a lot in common, huh?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Forgive me, but I must excuse myself, for the time of my appointment draws near. And in terms I'm sure you'll understand, a lanternless Ratnik is like a mapless traveler — a serious conundrum indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, sure! In that case, you go right ahead. We won't keep you any longer!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Not at all. Should the opportunity present itself, I'd gladly continue our conversation another time.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: You're always welcome to come visit my grave— Er, I mean, the grave I stand watch over. Your visit would bring much-needed light to that place of final rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Right... Well, uhh... If we get the chance...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Then allow me to wish you a traditional Ratnik's farewell: See you by the graveside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhhh... Jeez, what a weirdo.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to badmouth him and all — in fact, he seemed pretty cultured. But at the same time... kinda spooky? Must be all that time he's spent around graveyards...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you notice anything strange about his lantern?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: His lantern? Uhh... no, not really? You mean, 'cause it was broken?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Like there was something inside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Guess you've always had a nose for stuff like this... If you're worried, you can always ask him the next time we cross paths.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure thing. Guess that'll be... by the graveside?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't you start spouting all that weird stuff too!

choices.text: Forsaken in the wake of a calamity...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Paimon almost forgot something super important!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mm? Spit it out, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weren't we gonna go try out the Berries and Fried Meat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Must have left that craving by the graveside...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But now, heading all the way back to The Flagship feels like such a waste...
Please, accept today's boon. Come night or day, may the blessings of the Moon Goddess shine down upon you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on over there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looks like they're handing out food.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, free food!? Wow, the people here are so nice!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Quick, let's grab some too! Paimon's super curious what their food tastes like.
Moonlight illuminates the path before you, travelers from afar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How'd you know we were travelers?
Just now were asong the birds in the sky, singing of your wanderings. You are no ordinary guests, it seems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The birds in the... what now?
Forgive me, I should not have laid the words of others out as a welcome mat for our very first meeting. You, too, must be wondering who I am.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I am Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. Please, as do our followers and other passersby, accept today's boon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Happy to oblige! Paimon's name is Paimon, and this here is {NICKNAME}. Thank you so much for sharing your yummy food with us — we'll take one each.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You have our sincere gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Think nothing of it. These fruits were the finest we found, delicacies gathered in the wake of the morning dew. It is my hope that partaking of them may lift your spirits to heights anew.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The finest you found? Wow, that sure is kind of you, but... wouldn't you want to keep those for yourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ha... "The first fruit of the harvest must be placed upon the Moonlight Altar — not as an offering to the gods, but as a spark for lost hunters. For it is the blade of the starving that darkness most easily corrupts."

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As perhaps you have already heard, we Frostmoon Scions revere and worship the Moon Goddess. We believe that together, virtue and compassion are the shining light that will lead us all out of the long, dark night.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And now, with tides of haughty Fatui swarming into Nod-Krai, driven by greed, and greed alone... More than ever before, we must all unite under the banner of virtue.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Ha, look who it is again — those unsufferably "kind-hearted" Frostmoon Scions. Got enough for us, too?

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: That's right, two servings each! We're starving over here!

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: The Fatui... After what you've been doing to our sacred statues, how dare you even show your faces...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Vilemina, bestow today's boon upon our guests.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: You hear that? No slacking, now. We'll have the very best you've got.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: But... My Lady, they—

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please, you two, accept this meal. But remember this: "Kindness is the first lantern left to guide those who stumble in ignorance."

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Come again?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Let me finish. "But should they still refuse to follow the moonlit path, then by our frosted blades shall we show them its shadow."

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: ...You!

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Hey... Look who it is.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Tch, whatever. Just you wait — we'll be coming for you next.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Where's the meat? Who wants to eat this garbage?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, those stooges really are the worst.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Hmph... Ever since they came to Nod-Krai with all their weird equipment and built that so-called "Experimental Design Bureau," our lives have been turned completely upside down!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Judging from how they reacted just now... it seems the Fatui already know who you are, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Old grudges die hard...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we have gotten in their way in pretty much every nation we've visited, so we're probably at the top of their blacklist by now.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I see... then on behalf of the Frostmoon Scions, I thank you for the goodwill you have shown us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Eh? Why thank me?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Heh... Because, if they had gotten ahead of themselves just now, I'm sure you would have stepped in to help.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Just as the birds and beasts put it, your arrival heralds joy to us all. Besides, for a weary traveler far from home, what better respite than to bathe in the moonlight?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You will always be welcome at the Frostmoon Enclave, the place we call our home.

choices.text: Thanks for your kind invitation.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: May we meet again in the moon's gentle glow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mmm, these are delicious! So refreshingly fresh... Those two Fatui wouldn't know a good thing if it came up and bit them on the shoulder.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like Ineffa isn't done with her shopping yet, and the Adventurers' Guild is still empty. Where should we head next?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why don't we follow the map in the travel guide?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea! Wouldn't wanna let that kuuhenki down, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see... Okay! Paimon's got our route all figured out, so all that's left to say is... Don't fall behind!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is "Nuts 'N' Nuts"! It's mostly a fruit shop, but there's a Crafting Bench too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is the "Speranza", one of the travel guide's recommended restaurants. All the waiters here are kids!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is the "Vesnici Proleca Greenhouse"! Apparently, their flowers are all made of metal, so they'll never wilt away!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And this is the "Rossum Workshop"! If you ever need a weapon made, this is the place to go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And over here, they've got a super tall observation deck! Whoa, take a look at that! You can see really far out into the distance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That way's north, and that looks like... something built by the Fatui? And then, over there to the west... Ah, that must be the place Lauma mentioned, where the Frostmoon Scions live.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, so... Whaddya think? Even if Ineffa kinda stole her limelight earlier, this just goes to prove that Paimon's own tour guiding skills aren't too shabby either, right?

choices.text: Still not quite Ineffa level.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon, would it kill you to compliment Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Look, there must be someone at the Adventurers' Guild now. There's already a line forming outside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we'll finally be able to ask about your spaceship. Or was there anywhere else you wanted to stop by first?

choices.text: As a matter of fact...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where? Which one are y— Ohhh... Now you mention it, Paimon's noticed it too... Ugh, better not be who she thinks it is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, where we go first is completely up to you — either the Adventurers' Guild, or that suspicious-looking shop. A word of warning, though... If we step into that shop, be sure to keep a very close eye on your Mora!

choices.text: One of the storefront signs caught my eye...
You're the best, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, she sure is! It'd take hundreds of years of practice to beat the best tour guide in all of Teyvat!

choices.text: We'll swing by when we get a chance.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hehe... Please, here you go! And if you ever need anything else, don't forget to make the great Lord Sangemah Bay your first port of call!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh dear, so it is the real deal...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Of course it's the real deal! Everything you'll find here is one hundred and ten percent real, meaning every one of my deals is as real as a deal can— Wait a minute! ... Well, well, well, if it isn't my two most valued clients!

choices.text: Long time no see, Dori.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Hehe, and with no small thanks to your munificent patronage!

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Come, come, how could you just sneak into Nod-Krai like this without telling your dear Lord Sangemah Bay? If I'd known earlier, I would've made an absolute k— I mean, pulled out all the stops to ensure that your boat ride over was as comfortable as humanly possible!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank the Archons we didn't tell you...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh, come now! You know as well as anyone how impeccably and conscientiously above-board I am when it comes to doing business!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, regardless of whether that's true or not, the main issue here is that we had no idea you had a branch in Nod-Krai.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: A clever merchant always has a backup plan, or two, or three up their sleeves! As the saying goes: a rabbit with many burrows fears not the hunter's arrows, a merchant with stores galore hears no debtors at the door!

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Since you're both here in Nod-Krai, would you care for some of my finest local souvenirs? Whatever you're looking for, I have it! Or if it's Sumeru you're missing, I've got that covered too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We literally just arrived! Do we look like we're on the hunt for tourist trinkets to take back for our friends?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: My, my, your high-minded tastes never cease to impress! In that case, I know just the thing... You must be on the hunt for something like... this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's that? Your hat?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Information, of course! Information about Nod-Krai... locked securely in the otherwise impenetrable vaults of the Lord Sangemah Bay's brilliant mind.

choices.text: Now you mention it...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: I knew it! I just knew you'd appreciate the value of my wares... On the back of all our pleasant dealings in the past, I'll even take a hit by throwing in some insider info for free.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! You sure are feeling uncharacteristically generous today...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Wh—What do you mean by "uncharacteristically"? I'm the most generous person I— Ugh, forget it. Anyway, the long and the short of it is this...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: The moment I set up shop in Nod-Krai, it struck me how many different factions there were, all competing against each other for power and influence... Well, as they say, there's no time for business like a crisis.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Things got even more turbulent after the Fatui pulled down two Ancient Moon's Remnants... People began to catch a whiff of the coming chaos — and the more troubled the waters, the greater the potential profit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not at all sorry to interrupt, but we're not here for Mora.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh, really? But... Surely it was the tales of an adventurer's paradise that brought you here? The chance to take your very own slice of all the latest and greatest business opportunities!

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: In that case... What would you like to know about?

choices.text: What can you tell me about the Frostmoon Scions...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: The Frostmoon Scions? You mean, the people who believe in the Moon Goddess? They're not a "bad" bunch, it's just... Well, they have such simple tastes. No luxuries, no indulgences, no nothing! Trying to earn a little Mora from that lot is like trying to squeeze blood from a stone...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Still, things between them and the Fatui have gotten pretty tense. It's only a matter of time before the powder keg goes boom, and when that happens... that's when business will start to boom too, hehe.

choices.text: Please tell me about the Lightkeepers...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh, they're an organization set up to keep the locals safe. Apparently, they have a long and glorious history, and they're made up entirely of volunteers.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Pfft, but seriously — a volunteer organization, in Nod-Krai? This place is hardly a magnet for noble hearts. No pay, all work? That's not a business model, and it's certainly not for me...

choices.text: What can you tell me about the Frostmoon Scions...
Let's talk about the Fatui...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Everyone knows they're here for the Ancient Moon's Remnants, but no one's sure why they pulled them down in Nod-Krai, of all places.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Anyway, they've been acting mysterious enough, but if you ask me... That "Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau" of theirs up north hides secrets wilder still!

choices.text: Tell me what you know about the Knights of Favonius...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: That bunch of booze-loving Mondstadters? Ugh, don't even get me started.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: As fellow outlanders, I thought they'd be easy pickings, but somehow, every single one of our business negotiations wound up at The Flagship...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: I've done plenty of deals with heavy drinkers before, but those guys? I never once made it to the contract signing before blacking out. Ugh, I'm getting flashbacks of the hangovers just thinking about it...

choices.text: Would you know anything about a spaceship from the past...?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: A what now? A spaceship? Nope, never heard of anything like that...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Don't you two get involved in any big business here without so much as a heads up, you hear me? At the very least, consider letting me in as a key investor.

choices.text: Tell me what you know about the Knights of Favonius...
Let's talk about the Fatui...
I have no more questions...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Oh! I almost forgot to mention — sooner or later, you'll no doubt end up doing business with some other merchants in Nod-Krai, and someone's bound to mention a place called the "Curatorium of Secrets."

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Listen to my advice: Do not, under any circumstances, go there! No matter how much trouble you're in!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Curatorium of Secrets? What do they get up to there?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Just... a place that handles all kinds of disputes. But the owner will charge you an absolute fortune, and she has a temper to match. Nothing like your friendly neighborhood Lord Sangemah Bay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not just saying that to stop your competition from undercutting you... right?

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: (Ugh...! When did that little pipsqueak get so sharp? And after I gave them all that info for free, just to win them over...!)

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Wh—What do you mean? Of course not! I'm only thinking about your wallets — I mean, on behalf of your wallets!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're really not convincing anyone, you know...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Alright, alright... business is a cutthroat... business, I won't argue with that.

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: But I'm not lying about that boss lady — not only did she make it into my "Top Three People Not to Mess With in Nod-Krai," she's also in my "Top Three People Most Eager to Trade in Favors"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously? It feels like you're just badmouthing your rival now...

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: Fine! If you don't believe me, go see for yourselves! We might both be from Sumeru, but compared to hers, my conscience is so large, why, it could fill three whole Palaces of Alcazarzaray!

response.speaker: Dori
response.text: But when you realize what I'm saying is true, don't say that good old Lord Sangemah Bay didn't warn you!
