Set up a branch all the way out here in Nod-Krai, now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lucky us, the line seems to be gone now! C'mon, let's go say hi to Katheryne!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Katheryne! We meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne (?)
dialogues.text: Hah, how ridiculous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne (?)
dialogues.text: They often say that mortals, shackled by their own flesh and blood, may fail to perceive the truth of this world even when it is right beneath their very noses. Yet I had not expected to have the pleasure to witness such heights of absurdity firsthand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh, P—Paimon must've... gotten the wrong person? At second glance, you do seem a bit younger than Katheryne, and you certainly sound a lot less friendly...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne (?)
dialogues.text: Hah... A creator might forgive ignorance, but being mistaken for one of my own creations is beyond all pardon.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Look very closely, for standing before you is none other than Marionette, Seventh of the Fatui Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Harbinger!?

choices.text: Why are you even here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So all the Katherynes were made by Marionette? Does that mean the Fatui have been watching our every move?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But the Guild itself hasn't done anything shady, and Katheryne's only ever helped us... Better just stay alert going forward.)

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Tch... Today's encounter is merely a courtesy call... a friendly warning, if you will.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You interfered with my work once before, with that little robot. I let it slide — after all, it was nothing more than a distraction, a side project at best.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But we are in Nod-Krai now, and as such, I strongly advise you not to stand in the Fatui's way. Otherwise, the next time we meet, I might just have to drop all this meaningless etiquette.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh please, you've got some nerve coming out with barely veiled threats like that! You're the ones stirring things up here!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Oh, perhaps you have misunderstood? Just because Nod-Krai lacks a ruler at present, that does not mean it should not be ruled. We Fatui are simply... establishing a new order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, right! More like shady experiments, judging by your massive creepy research facility!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph... I've said what I came to say. What you do next, only you can decide — so why don't you start by using your already limited processing capacity to "calculate" your even more limited options?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And, being the refined young lady that I am, I shall indulge you just this once:

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Ad astra abyssosque! Welcome to Nod-Krai, dominion of the Fatui.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, Paimon's so mad right now! How can anyone so obviously evil be so annoyingly self-righteous?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if a Fatui Harbinger is here to greet us in person, that can only mean one thing...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...That they've been keeping a very close eye on us indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, we'll have to be extra careful from here on out... Gah, Paimon hates feeling like she's being watched!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, the real Katheryne's back!

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Ad astra abyssosque! Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: How may I help? I will do everything I can to assist you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aww, you're so much nicer to talk to, Katheryne! Please don't leave us again, okay?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hmm...?

choices.text: And more importantly, will you be the one handing out commissions from here on out?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I told you already, I'm not Katheryne! Just how obsessed are you with my machines?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me help!

dialogues.speaker: Liouba
dialogues.text: Alright! You just need to hit these 'bots in a short time... And don't worry, they'll be collecting fluid impact force data for me while you're at it.

dialogues.speaker: Liouba
dialogues.text: Hmm. As to how they'll be arrayed, I'll leave that up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hello. I was just about to start tracking your whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you manage to get everything Aino asked for?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I did. What about you? Do you need me to navigate or introduce any more places around town?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not for now — we've seen most of it already! We probably need some time to process everything we've learned, though.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Any progress with the spaceship?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No... Katheryne came back just now, so we asked her, but even she hasn't heard a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: One possible explanation is the vast stretch of time that has elapsed. Additionally, given the limited resources available in Nod-Krai, it is entirely plausible that the wreck was scrapped for parts, or even mistaken for a pile of broken machinery...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh*

choices.text: I'm prepared for that possibility...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. In that case, why don't we go ask Aino together?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: After all, she was the one who salvaged me — ancient dragon technology and all. If there really are any unusual parts floating around Nod-Krai, there's a high chance they've passed through her hands at some point or another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good point! And since you keep mentioning her, we're curious to meet this whiz-kid mechanic too!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Understood. Then I'll handle navigation as before. ETA at the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop: 34 minutes ahead of schedule.

choices.text: ...But still, I can't just give up before we've even started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no! There's a little animal trapped over there. Let's go help it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? That's weird... Why isn't it responding?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: The tides of kuuvahki affect everything in Nod-Krai — so much so that many creatures have evolved a kind of dependency upon it, growing stronger or weaker as it waxes and wanes. This little animal must have been caught here unprepared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're saying we need to use kuuvahki? Paimon'll leave it to you guys, then!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't be scared! We'll get you out of there soon.

talks.objective: Use kuuvahki to aid the trapped Finch
Go to the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Here we are, the place Aino and I call home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! So many machines that Paimon's never even seen before! And then there's all these little robots... Did Aino build them all?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That is correct. It looks like Aino has created three more little bots since I've been gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww... Well, you were gone for quite a bit. She must've missed you!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I missed her too. I want her to see what I've become.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's not keep her waiting any longer, then. C'mon!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino, I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Hmm...?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...! I—Ineffa, you're... back significantly earlier than I expected! Like... a whole thirty minutes, at least?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Everything went very smoothly, which saved me quite a bit of time. So I—

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino, could you turn around for a moment?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I—I've been on my best behavior, the whole time you've been gone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's got chocolate all over her mouth...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Aino. While I was away, did you strictly abide by my tailor-made snack intake schedule?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: O—Of course I did! One whole cake, one krumkake, and one pack of chocolates a day, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: It was "either" a cake, or a krumkake, or a pack of chocolates per day.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Oh shoot...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: When did you finish the snack stash I left for you?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Literally just earlier today...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Let me just go run a scan on that.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I meant today, a week ago...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: And then you restocked an entire week's worth on your own initiative?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Two weeks' worth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does Paimon feel like the roles in this household... are pretty much the opposite of what she imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Calculation complete. Aino's recommended snack calorie intake for the next four weeks: 0.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ehhh!? No fair! You're a meanie, Ineffa!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: This is what happens when you break an agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: C'mooon! Don't do this to me!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I only ate a tiny bit extra every day! Just a teensy, eensy, weensy bit extra!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: That is objectively not a "teensy" bit extra...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ugh, seriously! If you'd only arrived half an hour later, I would've had everything cleaned up, and you wouldn't have noticed a thing!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: But now that I think about it, you even said you'd come back a bit earlier than you did... so I wouldn't have to worry...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: But then... You were away so long, and I was so worried about you, and that's the only reason I even...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I am very sorry to have kept you waiting. I'm back now...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: *sob* Mm... Welcome home...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sob* Aww...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: So... Will I be able to keep eating snacks as usual now?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Negative.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Awww...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Okay... Well, given that I am later than I initially projected... I'll let it slide. But just this once.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Thanks, Ineffa! You're the best!

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Aino, allow me to introduce—

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: #It's Honorary Knight {NICKNAME} and Paimon! I know, I know — Uncle Varka talks about you guys all the time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice to meet you, Aino! Ineffa's told us all about you, too!

choices.text: The whiz-kid mechanic...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Heh, really? She actually said that about me?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Hehe... Well, she's not wrong!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Oh yeah, so... You're here to see Uncle Varka, right? A couple of days ago, he suddenly said he had to head out on business, and that he might not be back for a while. He asked me to let you know if I saw you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, we heard about that at The Flagship. Did he say what he was doing?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Nope! Just told me to take good care of you guys, and make sure you feel right at home... Oh, shoot! Uh, please, take a seat!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Do either of you need my help with anything? Anything at all! After all, I'm the head of this household!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Sure wouldn't know it from that snack tantrum she just threw...)

choices.text: Miss Aino...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: A spaceship, huh? From outside Teyvat?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! So... Ring any bells?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Ah... Nope!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... You sure?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Nope means nope! Never seen the slightest trace of it!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: More specifically, by "nope," I mean I've never seen a single piece of tech in all of Nod-Krai that might've come from out of this world. Not in any new machines, or in any old ones either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: What Aino means... is that your spaceship almost certainly has not been disassembled, nor repurposed as parts for other machines.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So that's what she was getting at...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Yup! I've taken apart pretty much all the fun stuff in this city at one point or another, but I don't recall ever seeing any components that were anywhere near that special!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: So either your spaceship crashed somewhere it's never been found, or someone DID find it and then hid it really, really well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But who would even do something like that...?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Beats me! Maybe someone who thought they could stash it away for a rainy day? Just like how I sometimes hide snacks in the— Ahem...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: A—Anyway... Long story short, I definitely haven't seen anything like that!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Besides, sounds like it would practically be ancient history by now! If anyone still has any leads on what really happened, it'd be the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Frostmoon Scions?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Huh? Haven't heard of them yet? Didn't Ineffa tell you about their rituals?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: There wasn't enough time to delve deeper into their history and traditions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What kind of rituals are we talking about?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: I've never actually seen them myself, just heard bits and pieces, here and there.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: They say that each of their Moonchanters has had access to an ancient relic that lets them "see" the true past.

choices.text: The true past...

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Not sure exactly how it's meant to work. I can't get my head around anything that can't be explained by either machines or science... and to tell you the truth, I don't like it much either!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like we'll have to try our luck with the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Aw, leaving so soon? Sure you don't wanna hang out a little longer?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: It's getting late, Aino, and these two still need to head over to Hiisi Island. It would not be convenient for them to linger much longer.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Aww... Alright then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, don't worry! We'll be sure to drop in on you as often as we can!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Really? You promise?

choices.text: Pinky promise.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Hehe, sounds like my type of visitors! You're welcome anytime!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I'll be staying to look after Aino today, so I won't be going with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't sweat it! We'll find our way just fine.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: I'm glad to hear that. Also... I must admit, I have very much missed the "charging bed" that Aino made for me.

choices.text: Next time, we'll bring you something tasty too.
You mean, they can see what really happened?
I wanted to ask you about... a certain spaceship...
Ineffa's nearest and dearest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seeing Ineffa and Aino reunited like that sure was heart-warming...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A real "family," huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm! We should definitely hang out with them more in the future!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of homes, we must already be close to where the Frostmoon Scions live. The vibe here feels different, just like the scenery...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what was that? Felt like some sort of breeze blew by, and then the petals suddenly turned into... Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that... a kuuhenki? She looks different from the ones we saw before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! What's your name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Doesn't seem able to speak.

choices.text: Need our help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No idea what she wants... Unless you wanna stop, maybe we should just keep moving?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...She's following us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Go on, go on now... We've got stuff to do. Best you find someone else to hang out with...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hey, you scared it off...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Don't make it sound like Paimon's some kind of... meanie!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon had no idea what she wanted, okay? Ugh... Anyway, next time Paimon sees her, Paimon promises she'll be nicer!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seeing as we're on our way over to meet Lauma anyway, we can ask her about it while we're there!

choices.text: Something you wanna show us?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Lauma, you have returned.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Vilemina, this is {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Kindly arrange for two additional dinner settings for our honored guests.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Of course, my Lady.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, everyone along the way here pretty much saluted you! Are you, like... super important around here?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I am but a Moonchanter, one entrusted to convey the Moon Goddess's will. Nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: She's just being modest! The Moonchanter holds the highest rank among us Frostmoon Scions. Lauma is our leader.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Vilemina...

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: I know, I know... I'll send word to the kitchen. Two meals coming up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Paimon had no idea you were such a big shot!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: It is merely that the unique traits of our bloodline have manifested themselves especially strongly in my person. That is no accomplishment of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please, follow me this way.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Even to this day, I am still trying to piece together the many fragments of our past. It is a story not only of the Frostmoon Scions, but also of the moons themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A story of the moons...?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. We Frostmoon Scions are the last descendants of the ancient golden realm of Hyperborea. Its former glory may have faded, but what remains is a memory uniquely ours.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: In the distant past, Teyvat had not just one moon, but three. It is said that they were created by the primordial master of this world, cast into the firmament to keep peace in the land below.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: First born was the Eternal Moon, largest of the three. Legend has it that it was her immense kuuvahki that gave rise to the ocean tides.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Next was the Frost Moon... Smaller than her big sister, yet brightest in radiance. Her glow became the cold, undying lantern of the night.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Finally came the Iridescent Moon, smallest of the sisters. Most of the time, her light was barely visible to the naked eye — yet when she shone, her fleeting halos were all the more mysterious for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, sounds like it all happened so long ago... So, what happened to them afterwards?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Afterwards... Well, as you have seen, the three Moon Goddesses perished. This happened in a war triggered by the Descenders, and of the three lunar husks, only the Frost Moon survived unbroken, while the others were shattered to pieces.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, so that's why there were Ancient Moon's Remnants in the sky...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yes. It is also said that when the moons shattered, most of their fragments rained down upon this land like stardust. That is why Nod-Krai is blessed with such an abundance of kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: As for the remnant that the Fatui recently pulled down... that belonged to the Eternal Moon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... But you just said that two of the moons were shattered, so... where are the remnants of the Iridescent Moon?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: The Iridescent Moon's remnants were never found. What happened to her after the war remains a mystery... Some say she vanished in an instant, while others believe that her remnants are simply too delicate to leave a trace.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Three moons... I wonder... which one was Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon related to?)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Yet though the era of the three moons has long since faded into legend, successive generations of Frostmoon Scions have always passed down a prophecy — that one day, the Moon Goddess would return.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And in the end, that prophecy did indeed come to pass, though not quite—

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Lady Lauma! Lady Lauma, are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Kapy? What is the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Lady Lauma, it's my daughter, Kaarina... Her illness...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Take me to her, right away.

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: *groan*

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Her sensitivity to kuuvahki is flaring up again... After her last treatment, did you follow my advice and seek medical help in Nasha Town?

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: But... But those doctors are all Snezhnayan! They're outsiders, compatriots of those brutes who invaded our homeland... How can we possibly trust them?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Not all outsiders are enemies, Kapy. They've been treating this condition for generations... They have the experience we lack.

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: But we're Frostmoon Scions! Should we not remember what the outsiders did to our moons? Surely, the Lady Kuutar will reward our devotion...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But Kapy, Kuutar is long... *sigh* This isn't the time for a debate.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: "...O lost child, snowswept and buffeted by the howling winds of the frigid night, let not the silver flame within you fade. By the Frost Moon's grace I shall warm you, curled up as a fledgling in frozen soil..."

dialogues.speaker: Kaarina
dialogues.text: *snore*

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Ah...! Praise be to the Moon Goddess! My Kaarina...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Remember, she must take powdered Lakkaberries daily. It will ease her symptoms.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Did she just use her own power to heal that girl...?)

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: ...Lauma.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Vilemina? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Dinner is ready.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Kapy, let her rest here for the night. I'll have someone bring her a blanket.

dialogues.speaker: Kapy
dialogues.text: Alright... Thank you so much, Lady Lauma!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will she be alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! If there's anything at all we can do, please don't hesitate to ask!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you for your kindness. For now, though, Kaarina should be fine... She'll be feeling a lot better tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Judging from what we just saw, that doesn't sound like a long-term solution...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...But I'm guessing that Lauma couldn't say anything else, at least in front of Kaarina's mother.)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Please, do not be worried. Come, let us head to dinner. I believe you still have some questions for me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: I... Oh, sorry. Yes, I'll be coming too. I was just... thinking about something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh?

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: *sigh* Lauma makes such an unshakable Moonchanter... Calm, capable, someone we can count on. Deep down, though, I know she's been quietly carrying the burden for the rest of us.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Believe me when I say that as a fellow Frostmoon Scion, I do worry about Lauma. It's just that sometimes... it's hard to say it to her face.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: Could I... ask you to look out for her? I can tell she really trusts you.

choices.text: Sure, but... I think you should just tell her straight.

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: I fear that would stress her out even more...

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: Sometimes, I really admire her strength... but at the same time, I can't help feeling powerless myself.

choices.text: Alright, I'll keep an eye out.

response.speaker: Vilemina
response.text: Thank you, it means a lot.

talks.objective: Have dinner with the Frostmoon Scions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... Paimon's so full. That was even better than the stuff you gave us before!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm glad to hear it. Thank you for accepting such simple hospitality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, we should be the ones thanking you! Seriously, that was seriously scrumptious!

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: How did you even manage to finish it? This slop's barely edible.

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Then again, I guess that's what you'd expect from savages.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's you! Those rude ol' Fatui we just met back in Nasha Town!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: My sincerest apologies. If you found the food we gave you earlier difficult to swallow, may I suggest taking a deep breath... and joining us? These delicacies might change your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: After all, I suspect that your previous meal may have been tainted with something... most unpalatable.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean... Tainted with what exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: With the bitter snobbery of those who call themselves "civilized."

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Why you...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't push your luck!

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Oh? Looking for a fight? Sure, I'd be more than—

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Hold it. We're not here to brawl... yet. We're here on official business.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Orders from above. We're here to deliver the Frostmoon Scions a warning... or rather, a final ultimatum.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: You have three days to hand over the relic and reveal the whereabouts of your so-called "Kuutar." If you fail to do so, the Fatui will immediately begin the cleansing of Hiisi Island — which, by the way, is a sovereign territory of the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Vilemina
dialogues.text: ...What insolence. Your demands are outrageous! For generations, this land has belonged to the—

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Dear guests, allow me to save you both time and trouble with a speedy reply. The Frostmoon Scions will never hand over anything to the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And to those who set foot on our land with ill intent, I say this — with your blood we shall draw an inviolable line in the snow. That applies to you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Oiva
dialogues.text: Tch. Stubborn savages, the lot of you.

dialogues.speaker: Ognjen
dialogues.text: Hmph... You'll pay for this, mark my words!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! If you're so tough, get back here and put 'em up! Hmph, guess all they're good for is running away.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry... You've had to put up with far too much unpleasantness today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, it's not your fault! We don't like bullies like them either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But still... they mentioned a "relic" and "Kuutar." What exactly could they be after?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About this "relic"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... So, this might not be the best time to bring this up, but we kinda have a favor to ask of you, Lauma...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I see... So your questions concern the sacred relic too. Please, do not hesitate to speak your mind — unlike those insolent intruders, you walk in the moonlight with open hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You stood by us when we needed your help, so it's only right that I return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But let us continue this conversation somewhere more fitting. As it happens, there's something I'd like to show you too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's spectacular...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar" was born here on Hiisi Island around five hundred years ago. As it just so happened, a priestess of the Frostmoon Scions witnessed the moment of her birth.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Instantly realizing that this was the prophesied rebirth, she quietly recorded the event and carved this statue to honor that miracle.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: According to legend, Kuutar's birth was accompanied by the sudden appearance of many kuuhenki, who wove the moonlight that bathed her into silken vestments fit for a goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's like it knows we're talking about it!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: From that day forth, the kuuhenki have been regarded as Kuutar's familiars. Some believe that their habit of guiding travelers to hidden treasure stems from an instinct — the same one that not only drives them to protect the Moon Goddess, but also to make her smile.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: After all, according to the records, Kuutar always looked lonely as she gazed up at the distant moon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Kuutar's whereabouts...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Kuutar left Hiisi Island before I was even born.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: According to the previous Moonchanter, the goddess was angered by our people's greed, and that is why she left us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did she go?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: No one knows what happened after she left. But just a few months ago, after those two Ancient Moon's Remnants fell from the sky, she was spotted on Hiisi Island once more.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And the Fatui have been harassing and threatening us ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Judging from what they've said... our Moon Goddess is actually their missing Harbinger — Columbina, "The Damselette."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Damselette!? But isn't she... number three amongst the Fatui Harbingers!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So she's actually... the Moon Goddess? Why would she join the Fatui, then?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: That, too, is a question I've struggled with. But even at the best of times, understanding other people's choices is difficult... let alone those of a goddess.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Plus...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Ah, forgive me. There I go again, rambling on about our history... But you came here to ask about the sacred relic, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon's not sure which part she's more curious about now...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Since ancient times, the Frostmoon Scions have had in our possession a special fragment of the Ancient Moon's Remnants — a piece in which I sense a power unlike any other.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Successive generations of Moonchanters have all detected a divine presence within it. We call this unique remnant... the "Moon Marrow."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard you can use it to see what happened... in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: What is it in particular that you seek from the past?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well basically, to cut a long story short, {NICKNAME} here's actually from outside of Teyv— Mmph!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Paimon must've just remembered the unfortunate link between the three moons and the Descenders... But right now, I shouldn't try to hide it.)

choices.text: I'm not from Teyvat... I'm a Descender.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Thank you... Your honesty is a sign of your trust — both in me and the Frostmoon Scions.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Unfortunately, though, I won't be able to use the Moon Marrow to shed light on your past just yet.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Our people revere the Moon Marrow as a sacred relic. I'm only permitted to retrieve it from the secret chamber in which it is hidden once a year, on Moon-{RUBY#[D]Kuunrukous}Prayer Night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, really... So, when's the next Moon-Prayer Night?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Judging from the tides this evening... a little less than two months.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Does that mean... the date changes every year?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: The ceremony is held on the night when the moon is closest to Teyvat.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: This is also when Nod-Krai's kuuvahki reaches its peak. Only then can the seal on the secret chamber be lifted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess we've got no choice but to wait...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I am truly sorry that I cannot help you sooner.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: But as the Moonchanter, I swear that I will do everything I can to help you find the answers you seek.

choices.text: Thank you, Lauma.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Think nothing of it. After all you've done for us, you deserve nothing less.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *yawn*... Who'd have thought today was only our first day in Nod-Krai? Feels like so much has happened already!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #If I may be so bold... What does "family" mean to you, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether}...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: If you were aware of something, a secret that could hurt your family... Would you be honest with them, or try to hide it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...A secret? Surely, keeping your family in the dark is never right...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #(But... come to think of it, it's not as if {M#Lumine}{F#Aether} hasn't been hiding things from me...)

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Oh, I'm... so sorry. That was a strange question... I didn't mean to put you on the spot.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...It's okay.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: I guess... I've just never met anyone with a story quite like yours before. I just suddenly had the urge to ask...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: *yawn*... It's getting late, and you two must be rather tired, too. Would you like to stay the night here on Hiisi Island? I can have someone prepare some lodgings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's alright! We've already got a room back at The Flagship, as it happens. Speaking of which, if you ever need us, feel free to come knocking!

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Do you need me to show you the way back?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No worries! It's quite a way, and you should get some rest too, Lauma. We'll make sure to be careful.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Understood, then I won't keep you. May your first night in Nod-Krai pass in stillness and peace.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Whatcha thinking? Sure was an eventful day, huh...

choices.text: A lot to think about, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The good news is, we're not at a dead end in the search for your spaceship yet. We can always learn more about this place while we wait... the usual drill, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... *yawn* Paimon's really getting sleepy now. If she gets too tired to fly back, you carry her, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, okay...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #({M#Lumine}{F#Aether}... my {M#little sister}{F#big brother}... I wonder what you're doing right now?)

choices.text: A lot of threads to unravel... and even more conflicts to resolve.
It means a lot.
I'm searching for the truth about me and my sibling's past...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Anyway, don't be a stranger now! We might be in Nod-Krai, but don't forget — Dori's doors are always open for you!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: There she goes again. Some things never change... Does she really think that'll do anything to fix the mess that is Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Uh... Boss? That stuff looks super tasty... Think I could grab some too?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Come night or day, may the blessings of the Moon Goddess shine down upon you.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Feeling comfortable?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: I am indeed. No bed in the world is as comfortable as this one.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Yes?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Want me to increase the charging rate?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Please, if you would. Thank you, Aino.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Ineffa.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...Hm, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I'm hungry...

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: In that case... Please enable Quick Charge mode.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Let's give them some space so they can rest...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't this the Adventurers' Guild? Why isn't anyone here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean the Katheryne in Nod-Krai actually gets to clock out...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's come back later.

dialogues.speaker: Maciej
dialogues.text: Lady Lauma, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Vanamo
dialogues.text: Come day or night, may the blessings of the Moon Goddess shine down upon you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, now that's one huge statue!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: This is a statue of our goddess — the Moon Maiden, Kuutar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It worked!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Off you go now, little one! Don't go getting yourself caught again!
